variants.core_twist: Each player has an identical twelve-card deck, which is their whole hand each round. After each of three rounds, players buy one upgrade from a market in order of fewest tricks, replacing a card in their deck with a stronger one or one with a move, such as 'wins ties' or 'counts as any suit'.

variants.title: After You
variants.hook: Spend a courtesy and insist that everyone else plays first.
variants.core_twist: Each player has two courtesy tokens. On your turn you may spend one to defer and play your card after everyone else in this trick; if several players defer, the latest to do so plays last. Unspent tokens are worth a point each.

variants.title: Cavalry's Coming
variants.hook: Every trick you lose brings up another reinforcement.
variants.core_twist: Two players. Each has a hand of eight and four face-down reserve cards. Whenever you lose a trick, turn one of your reserves face-up; face-up reserves may be played as if they were in your hand. Twelve tricks at a point each. Losing early buys options and gives your opponent a look at them.

variants.title: Sold!
variants.hook: Win the trick, then sell it to whoever wants it most.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a public collector card that doubles the value of one suit for them alone. After winning a trick, the winner may offer it for sale: each other player makes one open bid in points, and the winner may sell to the highest bidder or keep it.

variants.title: Merry-Go-Round
variants.hook: The winning card's number spins the carousel, and the winner gets wherever it stops.
variants.core_twist: Eight carousel spaces form a ring, each with an effect: gain two, lose one, choose trump, swap a card with the deck, take the lead from the winner. After each trick the pointer advances by the rank of the winning card and the winner takes that space's effect. Everyone can count ahead to see which rank lands where.

variants.title: Mix It Up
variants.hook: Orange follows red and it follows yellow.
variants.core_twist: The deck has three primary suits and three secondary suits. A secondary card belongs to both of its parent colours: it may follow either, and when it is led, players may follow with either parent or the same secondary. The highest card that legally followed wins.

variants.title: Short Fuse
variants.hook: A one-minute timer runs on whoever holds the lead.
variants.core_twist: A sixty-second sand timer is turned over only when the lead changes hands. If the sand runs out, the player holding the lead loses two points and the timer restarts. Every card must be played within a count of three. Winning several tricks in a row lets the fuse burn down on you.

variants.title: Hired Hands
variants.hook: Win the bid, then make an offer: who will work for you, and for how much?
variants.core_twist: The highest bidder names trump and a number of tricks, then openly offers a wage out of the contract's value. Opponents in turn may accept; the first to accept becomes the declarer's partner and their tricks count toward the contract. If nobody accepts, the declarer plays alone for double.

variants.title: Even Stevens
variants.hook: Add up the trick. Odd, the highest card wins. Even, the lowest.
variants.core_twist: When a trick is complete, add the ranks of every card in it. If the total is odd, the highest card of the led suit wins; if it is even, the lowest card of the led suit wins. The last player to the trick usually decides which.

variants.title: Fair Deal
variants.hook: Nobody can blame the cards: every player plays every hand.
variants.core_twist: Cards are played in front of their owner instead of into the middle, so each hand stays intact. After each round, every hand passes one seat left and is played again. With as many rounds as players, everyone plays each hand once, and each hand awards three points to whoever took the most tricks with it.

variants.title: Running Tab
variants.hook: Change your bid whenever you like, as long as you pay for it.
variants.core_twist: Each player marks an exact bid on a personal track and holds five chips. After any trick you may pay one chip into the pot to slide your marker one step. At the end of the round, players exactly on their bid score three and split the pot; chips you still hold are worth a point each.

variants.title: Stage Fright
variants.hook: Every part in the play has a job, and the parts keep changing hands.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. Role cards carry goals: the Lead needs three tricks or more, the Understudy exactly one, the Prompter none, the Villain the last trick. Tricks are tucked under the role that won them. Whenever a player wins a trick they swap role cards with the player of the lowest card, so tricks stay with roles while the players move between them.

variants.title: Tag Team
variants.hook: Tag out and your partner plays two cards for the team.
variants.core_twist: Four players in fixed pairs. Once per round each player may tag out on their turn instead of playing. Their partner must then play two cards to that trick, and the better one counts for the team. The player who tagged holds a spare card and plays the final trick without their partner.

variants.title: Frostbite
variants.hook: Play the lowest card and the cold takes another from your hand.
variants.core_twist: After each trick, the player of the lowest card of the led suit must freeze one card from their hand, placing it face-down and out of the round. Hands shrink unevenly, and a player with no cards left sits out the remaining tricks. Tricks are a point each, so the choice is which cards you can afford to lose with.

variants.title: Four Hands
variants.hook: Two players, four hands: your left hand and your right hand are partners.
variants.core_twist: Two players. Each holds a left hand and a right hand of seven cards on separate racks and may never move a card between them. Tricks are four cards, played in the order my left, your left, my right, your right, and the winning hand leads next. You are your own partner, and you know both halves.

variants.title: Home and Away
variants.hook: You own a suit. Win at home for one point, on someone else's ground for two.
variants.core_twist: Each player is assigned a home suit. When your home suit is led, your cards of it count two ranks higher. A trick you win with a card of your own suit scores one; a trick you win with a card of another player's home suit scores two.

sources.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring – Trick-Taking Game

variants.title: Don't Feed the Bear
variants.hook: A bear sits at the table and plays its best card every time. If it wins the most tricks, nobody wins.
variants.core_twist: A bear hand lies face-up and plays automatically in turn: always its highest legal card. Players score a point per trick as usual, but if the bear ends the round with the most tricks, nobody scores. Stopping the bear costs good cards, and everyone would rather someone else paid.

variants.title: Piggy Bank
variants.hook: The tricks you win aren't safe until you lose one on purpose.
variants.core_twist: Tricks you win sit unbanked in front of you. Whenever you play the lowest card of the led suit in a trick, you bank everything you have unbanked. If you win the final trick of the round, all your unbanked tricks are lost. You have to choose when to stop winning.

variants.title: Herding Cats
variants.hook: Every trick nudges the cat one step. Everyone wants it in a different basket.
variants.core_twist: A cat token starts in the centre of a cross-shaped board whose four arms match the four suits. After each trick the cat moves one step along the arm of the winning card's suit. Each player holds a secret basket card naming an arm. When the cat reaches the end of an arm the round stops and anyone with that basket scores five; tricks score one each.

variants.title: Last Orders
variants.hook: Ring the bell and the next trick is the last. Just don't win it.
variants.core_twist: Tricks score a point each. Any player who has just won a trick may ring the bell before leading: the trick they now lead is the final one of the round, and whoever wins it loses three points. Unplayed cards are thrown in. The bell-ringer has to lead something they are sure to lose.

variants.title: Crescendo
variants.hook: The first trick is worth one, the second two, the seventh seven. Then the conductor drops the baton.
variants.core_twist: A round has eight tricks. The first is worth one point, the second two, and so on up to seven for the seventh. The eighth and last trick is worth nothing. You want your best cards late, but not last, and so does everyone else.

variants.title: Loser Buys the Round
variants.hook: Everybody collects penalties. Only the one with the most pays for them.
variants.core_twist: Tricks score a point each. Penalty cards are counted at the end of the round, and only the player holding the most of them loses points, one per card. Everyone else's penalties are forgiven. If players tie for most, they all pay.

variants.title: Spinning Plates
variants.hook: Three plates are wobbling. Every trick saves one and lets the others slip.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. Three of the four suits each have a plate on a track starting at four. After every trick each plate drops one step, except the plate of the winning card's suit, which goes back to four. A plate at zero smashes and the team loses. The fourth suit is trump and saves nothing. Survive ten tricks.

variants.title: Own Goal
variants.hook: Win a trick you led yourself and it counts against you.
variants.core_twist: A trick you win when following scores a point. A trick you win with the card you led costs you a point. The lead becomes something to get rid of, and a leader's best card is one that somebody will be forced to beat.

variants.title: Slips and Ladders
variants.hook: The card you win with is the number you move, so pick the one that lands on a ladder.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a pawn on a forty-space board of ladders and slides. Cards run from one to six in four suits. The trick winner moves forward exactly the rank of their winning card and then follows any ladder or slide they land on. Nobody else moves.

variants.title: Head Above Water
variants.hook: The tide rises one step each trick. Play anything below it and you go under.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. A tide marker starts at one and rises by one after every trick. Any card played with a rank below the tide costs the team one of three lifebelts. Low cards must be used early, while the lead and the need to follow suit conspire to keep them in hand.

variants.title: Sealed Lead
variants.hook: Everyone can see what suit was led. Nobody knows how high until the trick is over.
variants.core_twist: Card backs show their suit. The leader plays face-down, so the suit to follow is known but the rank is hidden. Everyone else plays face-up, and then the lead is turned over. A mighty-looking response may have been spent on a 2.

variants.title: Fine by Me
variants.hook: You may break suit any time you like. It costs a chip, and the trick winner collects.
variants.core_twist: Everyone starts with five chips, worth a point each. You may play off-suit even when you could follow, by putting a chip on the trick; the trick's winner takes all chips on it. A player with no chips must follow suit.

variants.title: Lucky Coin
variants.hook: One coin on the table adds five to a card. Win with it and you have to hand it over.
variants.core_twist: There is a single coin. Its holder may place it on any card they play to add five to its rank. If that card wins the trick, the coin passes to the player who played the lowest card; if it loses, the holder keeps the coin. Everyone can see who has it.

variants.title: Food Chain
variants.hook: Sharks beat seals, seals beat fish, fish beat plankton. Until the shark wins and sinks to the bottom.
variants.core_twist: The four suits sit in a ranked column and any card of a higher suit beats any card of a lower one, though you must still follow the suit led. Whenever a suit wins a trick, its tile drops to the bottom of the column and the others move up. The strongest suit is always the one that has waited longest.

variants.title: Moving Day
variants.hook: Load the van together: each of you must win with smaller and smaller cards.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. Each player keeps the cards they win tricks with in their own stack. Every winning card you add must be lower than the one on top of your stack; if it is not, a box is broken. The team needs the number of tricks on the job card with no more than two breakages, and nobody may discuss their hand.

variants.title: Do-Over
variants.hook: Once a round, shout 'do-over': everyone takes their card back and the trick starts again.
variants.core_twist: Each player has one do-over token per round. After a trick is complete but before it is collected, any player may spend theirs: all cards return to their owners' hands and the trick is replayed with the caller leading. Everyone has now seen one card from every hand.

variants.title: Leapfrog
variants.hook: Win a trick and your frog hops forward, right over anyone in the way.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a frog on a single line of lily pads. The trick winner's frog hops one pad forward, and if that pad is occupied it leaps on to the next empty one, clearing a whole queue in a single jump. The player of the lowest card slides back one pad. First to the pond wins.

variants.title: Hard Pass
variants.hook: You won the trick. Do you actually want it?
variants.core_twist: Cards carry plus and minus values. The trick winner may decline the trick, in which case it is offered to the next-highest card of the led suit, and so on down. The last player in line cannot refuse. Whoever takes the trick leads the next one.

variants.title: Reinvest
variants.hook: Spend a trick you've already won to make the card you're playing a trump.
variants.core_twist: There is no trump suit. When you play a card, you may turn one of your captured tricks face-down to make that card a trump for this trick. A spent trick no longer scores. Two trumps in one trick are ranked by their printed numbers.

variants.title: Soapbox Derby
variants.hook: Every trick you win makes your cart faster. The finish line is short and there's a wall behind it.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a cart on a hill and a speed dial starting at one. After every trick all carts roll forward by their speed. The trick winner then adds one to their speed and the player of the lowest card takes one off. A cart that stops inside the three-space finish zone scores by order of arrival; a cart that rolls past it has crashed and scores nothing.

variants.title: What's My Number?
variants.hook: Everyone can see how many tricks you need to win, except you.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. Each player's target for the round is chosen by the player on their left and placed in a stand facing outward, so you see every target but your own. The team wins if all players finish exactly on their targets. Nobody may speak about numbers; you work out your own from how the others play around you.

variants.title: Podium
variants.hook: Don't bid how many tricks. Bid where you'll finish, and nobody else can take your step.
variants.core_twist: Starting with the lowest scorer, each player puts their token on one step of a podium to predict their place in this round's trick count: first, second, third or last. Each step holds one token. Finishing exactly where you stood scores four; tied places count for the lower step.

variants.title: Gentlemen's Agreement
variants.hook: Agree out loud how to split the tricks. Then see who keeps their word.
variants.core_twist: Before play, the table negotiates openly how the round's tricks will be divided, with the shares adding up to the total. Each player's agreed share is their target. Finishing on your target scores three plus your tricks; missing it scores nothing. Everyone can succeed together, and one player breaking the deal sinks someone else.

variants.title: Good Fences
variants.hook: You share one score pile with the player on your left and another with the player on your right.
variants.core_twist: A shared pile sits between each pair of neighbours. When you win a trick you add it to the pile on your left or your right. At the end you score the smaller of your two piles. You need both neighbours to prosper, and they each have another neighbour to think about.

variants.title: Three at a Time
variants.hook: Forget bidding the whole hand. Just call the next three tricks.
variants.core_twist: Nine tricks are played in three sets of three. Before each set, all players show zero to three fingers at once: the number of the next three tricks they will win. An exact call scores two. You bid three times a round with more known each time.

variants.title: Checkout
variants.hook: Count down from fifty-one with your winning cards and finish on exactly zero.
variants.core_twist: Every player starts on fifty-one. When you win a trick, subtract the rank of your winning card from your score. The first player to land on exactly zero wins. A winning card that would take you below zero is a bust: your score does not change and you lose the lead to the player on your left.

variants.title: Daisy Chain
variants.hook: Each winning card has to match the last one, by colour or by number.
variants.core_twist: The card that wins each trick is added to a chain in the middle of the table. It must share a suit or a rank with the previous winning card. A player who wins a trick with a card that matches neither breaks the chain and takes a thorn worth minus two. Tricks score one each.

variants.title: Close but No Cigar
variants.hook: The winner takes the lead. The runner-up takes the cards.
variants.core_twist: The highest card of the led suit wins the lead and nothing else. The second-highest card of the led suit must take the trick's cards, and each smoke card among them is minus one. If only one card of the led suit was played, its owner takes the cards. You want to win outright or lose badly.

variants.title: Mouse and Elephant
variants.hook: The elephant beats everything except the mouse.
variants.core_twist: In each suit the highest card is the elephant and the lowest is the mouse. Normal ranking applies with one exception: if the mouse and the elephant of the same suit are in the same trick, the mouse wins it and the trick scores three instead of one.

variants.title: Slipstream
variants.hook: Tuck in one rank behind the winner and share the trick.
variants.core_twist: If a card in the trick is exactly one rank below the winning card and of the same suit, its player also scores the trick. Both get the point; the winner still leads. Holding the card just under an opponent's ace is as good as holding the ace.

variants.title: Villain of the Week
variants.hook: Each round one of you is the villain, with a nasty power and everyone else against you.
variants.core_twist: The villain role passes round the table. The villain draws a power card, such as 'your 1s are trumps' or 'you play last to every trick', and scores two per trick. The heroes score one per trick, and if the villain ends with fewer tricks than every hero, each hero scores two more.

variants.title: Party Pooper
variants.hook: If everyone follows suit, high card wins. One off-suit card and it's the lowest.
variants.core_twist: When every player follows suit, the highest card wins as usual. If anyone plays off-suit, the trick flips: the lowest card of the led suit wins. No trumps. A player who is out of a suit decides who wins tricks in it without ever winning one.

variants.title: Take a Number
variants.hook: Every bid can be made once. If someone has taken your number, pick another.
variants.core_twist: Six tickets numbered zero to five lie on the table. In turn from the dealer's left, each player takes one ticket, which is their exact bid for the round. No number can be taken twice. Making your ticket scores its number plus three.

variants.title: Best and Worst
variants.hook: Name your best card and your worst card before you start. Then prove it.
variants.core_twist: After the deal, each player places one card face-down under a Best token and one under a Worst token. They stay in your hand to be played when you choose. The Best card scores three if it wins the trick it is played to, and the Worst scores three if it is the lowest card in its trick. Tricks are a point each.

variants.title: Three Wishes
variants.hook: Everyone gets the same three wishes. Each works once all game.
variants.core_twist: Each player has three wish tokens for the whole game. Undo: after everyone has played, take your card back and play a different legal one. Crown: your card is the highest of its suit this trick. Swap: exchange a card in your hand with the top card of the deck. A spent wish is gone for good.

variants.title: Ballot Box
variants.hook: Everyone votes for trump with a card from their hand. The card is gone either way.
variants.core_twist: Before play, each player puts one card face-down in the ballot box. The votes are revealed together and the suit with the most votes is trump; a tie means no trump this round. The voting cards are out of the round, so backing your long suit costs you a card from it.

variants.title: Cruising Altitude
variants.hook: Win and you climb, lose badly and you sink. You only score while you're level in the clouds.
variants.core_twist: Each player has an altitude marker from zero to five. Winning a trick raises it by one and playing the lowest card of the led suit lowers it by one. After every trick, each player whose marker is on two or three scores a point. Too many wins take you out of the scoring band just as surely as too few.

variants.title: Pass the Buck
variants.hook: Stuck with a penalty? Slip it into the next trick you lose.
variants.core_twist: Penalty cards you capture lie face-up in front of you. Whenever you fail to win a trick, you may add one of your penalty cards to it before the winner collects. Penalties keep moving round the table, and the place to be at the end is the player who lost the last few tricks.

variants.title: Hot Goods
variants.hook: Someone is holding the stolen diamond. Catch them before they've kept it for six tricks.
variants.core_twist: One card in the deck is the diamond. If its holder still has it in hand after the sixth trick, they reveal it and score five. Before that, any player who wins a trick may accuse one opponent: if that player holds the diamond they must show it and lose three, and a wrong accusation costs the accuser one.

variants.title: Pay It Forward
variants.hook: Win a trick and give one of its cards away. Gifts are worth more than what you keep.
variants.core_twist: The trick winner keeps the trick but must give one card from it to another player as a gift. At the end, each card you kept scores one, each gift you gave scores one for you, and each gift you received scores two. You may not give to the same player twice running.

variants.title: Pinky Promise
variants.hook: You and each neighbour secretly agree which of you will win more. If you both say the same and it happens, you both score.
variants.core_twist: Each pair of neighbours shares a promise. Before play, both secretly choose which of the two will take more tricks, and the choices are revealed at the end. If they chose the same player and were right, both score two. Every player is in two promises, one on each side.

variants.title: X Marks the Spot
variants.hook: Win a trick and peek under one treasure tile. Take it, or put it back and remember.
variants.core_twist: Twelve face-down tiles are worth from minus two to plus four. The trick winner secretly looks at one tile and either keeps it or returns it to its place. The player of the lowest card may swap the positions of any two tiles without looking. What you remember, and what someone has just moved, decides what the next trick is worth.

variants.title: Queue Jumpers
variants.hook: Tricks don't score. Your place in the queue does.
variants.core_twist: Pawns stand in a queue in random order. After each trick, the winner swaps places with the pawn directly ahead and the player of the lowest card swaps with the pawn directly behind. When the hand ends the front of the queue scores four, then three, two and one.

variants.title: Trick or Lead
variants.hook: Win the trick and choose: keep the point, or keep the lead. Your opponent gets the other.
variants.core_twist: Two players. The winner of each trick chooses one of two things: score the trick, or lead the next one. Whichever they leave goes to the loser. Thirteen tricks, with a trump suit. Points and control never go to the same player twice in a row unless you allow it.

variants.title: One Trick Pony
variants.hook: Three cards, one round of betting, one trick. Winner takes the pot.
variants.core_twist: Each hand is a single trick. Players are dealt three cards and ante a chip. The dealer leads face-up. In turn, each other player folds or adds a chip to stay in; those who stay then play one card each, following suit if they can. The highest card of the led suit takes the pot.

variants.title: Shield Wall
variants.hook: Each invader has a number. Together, in one suit, you have to match it.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. An invader card with a strength is turned up for each trick. The leader picks the suit, and the invader is beaten only if the ranks of all cards played in the led suit add up to its strength or more; off-suit cards add nothing. As suits run dry, the wall thins. Three breaches lose.

variants.title: Paint by Numbers
variants.hook: Every card you play colours in a piece of your picture, and the trick winner colours two.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a picture sheet divided into regions marked with a colour and a number. After every trick, each player may colour one region matching the suit and rank of the card they just played, and the trick winner may colour a second matching any card in the trick. Finished objects in the picture score.

variants.title: Light and Heavy
variants.hook: The card backs tell everyone whether a card is high or low, but not its suit.
variants.core_twist: Cards ranked one to five have a light back and cards ranked six to ten a dark back. Everyone can see how many strong cards each player still holds, but no suits. Play is ordinary must-follow with exact bids, made in full view of each other's weight.

variants.title: Bumper Cars
variants.hook: The more people who follow suit, the further the winner drives, and anyone in the way gets shunted.
variants.core_twist: Cars circle a twelve-space track. The trick winner drives forward one space for every card of the led suit in the trick. A car that lands on an occupied space bumps the other car back two spaces. Each completed lap is worth three points.

variants.title: First Past the Post
variants.hook: Five public races. Each is won by whoever does it first.
variants.core_twist: Five race cards are laid out: first to win tricks with three different suits, first to win with a 1, first to win two tricks in a row, first to win a trick without trump being played, first to lose three tricks running. Each scores three for the first player to do it. Tricks themselves score nothing.

variants.title: Top of the Heap
variants.hook: Win a trick and climb. Whoever was standing there goes down.
variants.core_twist: A hill has five levels with room for one climber on each above the base. The trick winner climbs one level. If someone is already there, that player is knocked down a level, and knocks down anyone below them in turn. At the end of the hand you score the level you stand on.

variants.title: Over the Fence
variants.hook: A card sits on the fence between you and each neighbour. Either of you can play it.
variants.core_twist: One face-up card lies between each pair of neighbours. On your turn you may play a fence card from your left or your right instead of a card from your hand, following suit as if it were yours. A used fence card is replaced from the deck after the trick.

variants.title: Dance Card
variants.hook: Before the music starts, book a partner for particular tricks.
variants.core_twist: A round has eight numbered tricks. Before play, players pencil in partners: any two may agree to dance a specific trick together, and each player may book up to three. In a booked trick, if either partner wins, both score a point. Unbooked tricks score for the winner alone.

variants.title: Going Up?
variants.hook: One lift, nine floors. An odd card sends it up, an even card sends it down.
variants.core_twist: A lift marker starts on the fifth of nine floors. After each trick it moves up one floor if the winning card is odd and down one if it is even. Each player holds a secret floor ticket. If the lift is on your floor at the end of a trick you may show the ticket, score four and draw a new one. Tricks have no other value.

variants.title: Pass It Round
variants.hook: After every single trick, everyone passes a card to the left.
variants.core_twist: When a trick is finished, each player passes one card from their hand to the player on their left before the next lead. Hands never settle, you always know one card your neighbour holds, and you are always holding one your other neighbour wanted rid of.

variants.title: Bumper Crop
variants.hook: The crop everyone grows is worthless. The one nobody grows is gold.
variants.core_twist: A tally board counts how many tricks each suit wins. At the end of the round, tricks won by the suit that won the most are worth nothing, tricks won by the suit that won the fewest (but at least one) are worth three each, and all others one. You are steering the market and your own harvest at once.

variants.title: Silent Running
variants.hook: Hide one of your own cards as your submarine. Every winning card is a depth charge.
variants.core_twist: Before play each player sets aside one card from their hand face-down: its suit and rank are where their submarine is hiding. Each trick's winning card is a depth charge that hits any submarine of the same suit within one rank. A hit player says so and loses three points. Tricks score one each.

variants.title: Form Guide
variants.hook: Tip the player who'll win the most tricks and the one who'll win the fewest. Neither can be you.
variants.core_twist: After looking at their own hand, each player secretly sets two tip tokens: which opponent will take the most tricks this round and which the fewest. Each correct tip scores two and tricks score one each. You know your own hand's strength and nothing else, and your play can push the result.

variants.title: Fair Shares
variants.hook: The winner splits the trick into two piles. The loser chooses first.
variants.core_twist: Cards carry point values, some negative. The trick winner divides the cards of the trick into two piles of any size. The player who played the lowest card picks one pile and the winner keeps the other.

variants.title: On a Budget
variants.hook: Every card costs its own number to play, and you have forty to spend.
variants.core_twist: Each player has a budget dial set to forty. Playing a card costs its rank. Eight tricks are played from a hand of ten. Once you cannot afford a card you must play it face-down as a zero that cannot win. A hand of high cards is expensive to run.

variants.title: Opposite Day
variants.hook: Whoever is losing decides whether tricks are good or bad this round.
variants.core_twist: After the deal, the player in last place looks at their hand and declares the round: tricks are worth a point each, or tricks cost a point each. Everyone else has to play the hand they were dealt under a rule chosen to suit somebody else's.

variants.title: Cover Charge
variants.hook: It costs a chip to lead. Win your own lead and you get it back with interest.
variants.core_twist: Everyone starts with six chips, which are points. The leader must put a chip on their lead card. The trick winner takes any chips in the trick plus one from the bank. Winning as a follower gains two; winning your own lead gains one; leading and losing costs one.

variants.title: Honourable Mention
variants.hook: The best card that didn't win gets a ribbon. Three ribbons beat a trick.
variants.core_twist: The trick winner scores a point. The highest card of the led suit that did not win earns its player a ribbon. At the end of the round each set of three ribbons scores two points. A hand of kings under other people's aces has its own way to score.

variants.title: Blind Date
variants.hook: Two of you are partners this round. You won't find out who until both hearts are played.
variants.core_twist: Two cards in the deck carry a heart. Their holders are secret partners and score the product of their two trick counts; each other player scores their own tricks doubled. Neither partner knows who the other is until a heart card is played.

variants.title: Wolf and Shepherd
variants.hook: The shepherd counts tricks. The wolf only wants the sheep.
variants.core_twist: Two players, asymmetric. Five cards in the deck are sheep. The shepherd wins the round by taking seven of the thirteen tricks. The wolf wins by capturing tricks containing three of the five sheep, however few tricks that takes. Each side holds some of the sheep and decides when to risk them.

variants.title: All Hands on Deck
variants.hook: Your tricks count only if you've won with every suit.
variants.core_twist: The cards you win tricks with stay face-up in front of you. Tricks are a point each, but you score them in full only if your winning cards include all four suits. With three suits you score half, and with fewer nothing. A hand strong in one colour has work to do.

variants.title: Arch-Rivals
variants.hook: Any trick is worth a point. Beating your rival's card is worth two.
variants.core_twist: Each player's rival is the player on their left. A trick scores one point, or two if your winning card beat a card of the same suit played by your rival. Around the table everyone is hunting one neighbour and hunted by the other.

variants.title: House Conventions
variants.hook: You can't talk about your cards. But before each mission, you may agree one secret signal.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative campaign. Table talk about hands is forbidden, but before each mission the team may write one new convention on a shared card, such as 'leading a 2 means I have no trumps'. Conventions stay for the rest of the campaign, and later missions cannot be beaten without the language the team has built.

variants.title: Best Foot Forward
variants.hook: When you lead, you must lead the highest card you have in that suit.
variants.core_twist: The leader chooses any suit but must lead their highest card in it. Followers play freely within the suit. Having the lead forces out your top cards one suit at a time, so winning a trick costs you the best card of whichever colour you turn to next.

variants.title: Pick Your Poison
variants.hook: Build your hand one card at a time from two piles, seeing each card's suit but not its number.
variants.core_twist: There is no deal. Card backs show suits. In turn, each player takes the top card of either of two face-down piles until hands are full, knowing the suit they are taking and nothing more. Then a normal must-follow round is played with exact bids. You can build a void or a long suit; you cannot know if it is any good.

variants.title: Most Wanted
variants.hook: After each round, the table votes on who is most dangerous. That player starts the next round with their hand showing.
variants.core_twist: At the end of each round all players vote at once for the most dangerous player at the table. Whoever receives the most votes plays the first three tricks of the next round with their hand face-up. The handicap is assigned by opinion, not by score.

variants.title: Top This
variants.hook: The trick isn't finished after one card each. Add a second to raise.
variants.core_twist: After everyone has played one card, players in turn may add a second card of the same suit as their first; the two count as their sum. Raising continues until everyone passes, and nobody may add a third. A card spent raising is a card you will not have later.

variants.title: Captain of the Day
variants.hook: One player leads every trick this round, whoever wins.
variants.core_twist: The captain leads all the tricks of the round, and the role moves one seat each round. Winning a trick scores a point and gives no control. The captain can strip a suit from the table at will; everyone else knows exactly where they sit in every trick.

variants.title: Calling the Next One
variants.hook: Throw away this trick to bet that you'll win the next.
variants.core_twist: On your turn you may play your card face-down as a wager instead of into the trick. It cannot win and need not follow suit. If you win the next trick you score two extra points; if not, you lose one. You give up one trick to make another count triple.

variants.title: Half-Time
variants.hook: Two bids, not one: how many tricks before the break, and how many after.
variants.core_twist: A round is ten tricks with a pause after the fifth. Before play, each player bids two exact numbers, one for each half. Each half you hit scores three and hitting both scores two more. A hand that is all early winners or all late ones has to be bid that way.

variants.title: The Golden Ticket
variants.hook: One card wins the round outright for whoever captures it.
variants.core_twist: A golden ticket card is shuffled into the deck and counts as the lowest card of its suit. Whoever wins the trick containing it wins the round at once for five points; tricks score one each only if the ticket was never dealt. Its holder must choose the trick in which to let it go.

variants.title: Pencilled In
variants.hook: Everyone books one trick in advance where their suit will be trump.
variants.core_twist: Before play, each player places a token on one trick number of the round track and names a suit. In that trick, that suit is trump. Two bookings on the same trick cancel each other. The schedule is public, so everyone can plan around when each trump arrives.

variants.title: Harvest Festival
variants.hook: Four crops, four ways to score: you can't chase them all.
variants.core_twist: Captured cards are sorted by suit and each suit scores by its own rule. Apples score one per card. Pumpkins score five to whoever holds the most and nothing to anyone else. Corn scores three for every set of three. Thistles cost one each unless you hold all of them, when they score ten.

variants.title: Next-Door Duels
variants.hook: There's no winner of the trick. You just have to beat the neighbour on each side.
variants.core_twist: After a trick, each player compares their card with the card of the player on their left and on their right, and scores a point for each neighbour they beat by normal rules. The player who won the most duels leads. One trick can pay out to several people.

variants.title: Half and Half
variants.hook: Half your hand is yours. The other half was packed for you by the player on your right.
variants.core_twist: Ten cards are dealt to each player. Everyone keeps five and passes the other five to the left, so each hand is half chosen by its owner and half by a neighbour. The round is a penalty game, so what you give away matters as much as what you keep.

variants.title: Your Call
variants.hook: Trump is named after the lead is on the table, by a caller who changes every trick.
variants.core_twist: A caller token moves one seat clockwise each trick, independently of who wins. Once the leader has played, the caller names the trump suit for that trick, then play continues. The leader commits before knowing trump; the caller chooses knowing the lead and their own hand.

variants.title: Plea Bargain
variants.hook: Before the hand, plead innocent, petty or guilty to the penalties you're about to collect.
variants.core_twist: Twelve penalty cards are worth minus one each and one is minus four. Each player secretly pleads: Innocent (no penalty points), Petty (one to three) or Guilty (four or more). A correct Innocent plea scores four and a correct Petty plea two. A correct Guilty plea cancels all the penalties that player took.

variants.title: Bucket List
variants.hook: Five things to do before the round ends, and you must do them in order.
variants.core_twist: Each player is dealt a list of five tasks to complete in sequence, such as 'win with a red card', 'play the lowest card in a trick', 'win the trick straight after losing one'. Only the top unfinished task can be ticked off. Each completed task scores its position, from one to five.

variants.title: Party Planners
variants.hook: Five days, five house rules, and the players decide which rule falls on which day.
variants.core_twist: Five rule cards are revealed at the start, such as 'lowest card wins', 'no trumps today' or 'the last trick is worth five'. Taking turns, players assign each rule to one of the five rounds on a calendar. The whole schedule is fixed and visible before the first deal, and each player has shaped part of it.

variants.title: Silver Linings
variants.hook: Every penalty card you're stuck with gives you a small favour next round.
variants.core_twist: Each penalty card costs one or two points and also shows a consolation that its holder may use once in the following round: look at one opponent's hand, lead the first trick, pass an extra card, or ignore one penalty. Taking a bad trick now is a loan against the next hand.

variants.title: Trick Shots
variants.hook: Three trick shots are on display. Win a trick that looks like one and take the trophy.
variants.core_twist: Three shape cards are face-up, each describing a kind of trick and a bonus: all one suit, total under twelve, contains a pair, won by the lowest trump. The first player to win a trick of that shape claims the card for its bonus and a new one is revealed. Plain tricks score one.

variants.title: Lucky Sevens
variants.hook: Trump isn't a suit. It's a number, and the die picks it.
variants.core_twist: At the start of each round a die sets the lucky number. Every card of that rank is a trump and belongs to no suit; trumps rank among themselves in a fixed suit order. All other cards follow suit normally. Each round a different four cards rule the deck.

variants.title: Second Price
variants.hook: Win the auction and you only have to make the runner-up's bid.
variants.core_twist: Players bid a number of tricks in one round of open bidding. The highest bidder names trump and becomes declarer, but their contract is the second-highest bid made. Making it scores that number plus two; failing loses it. Everyone else scores a point per trick.

variants.title: Set List
variants.hook: Arrange your whole hand in order before the round, then play it three cards at a time.
variants.core_twist: After the deal, each player stacks their ten cards face-down in an order of their choosing. You hold only the top three. After playing a card you draw the next from your stack. The plan is made before the first lead, and the play is making it fit what everyone else planned.

variants.title: Any Questions?
variants.hook: You may not discuss your hand. You may ask one yes-or-no question per trick.
variants.core_twist: Cooperative. Before each trick, the leader may ask one teammate a single yes-or-no question, which must be answered truthfully. No other talk about cards is allowed. The team must complete the task cards for the mission, and the craft lies in choosing the one question worth asking.

variants.title: Second Thoughts
variants.hook: The leader gets to see what everyone played, then change their mind.
variants.core_twist: After all other players have played to the trick, the leader may take back the card they led and replace it with another card of the same suit. The lead becomes the strongest seat at the table, and the trick winner inherits it.

variants.title: Uncovered
variants.hook: Both hands are face-up in overlapping rows. You can only play a card with nothing on top of it.
variants.core_twist: Each player's twelve cards are dealt face-up in a pyramid of overlapping rows, as in a patience game. Only uncovered cards may be played, and playing one may free the cards beneath. Must-follow applies to your available cards. All information is open; the question is which cards you can reach and when.

variants.title: Lopsided
variants.hook: One suit has five cards and another has fourteen.
variants.core_twist: The four suits have five, eight, eleven and fourteen cards, each numbered from one. The five-card suit is trump. Everyone knows how scarce each suit is, so voids are common in the short suits, and the 11 in the long suit is a middling card.

variants.title: Hand-Me-Downs
variants.hook: The two cards you didn't play this round go to the player below you.
variants.core_twist: Each round, ten cards are dealt and eight tricks played. Your two unplayed cards are passed to the player ranked immediately below you on the scoreboard, who adds them to their next hand and discards two others. The leader chooses what to hand down; last place receives and gives nothing.

variants.title: Second Opinion
variants.hook: The leader plays first, but the second player decides the suit.
variants.core_twist: The suit that must be followed is set by the second card played to the trick, not the first. The leader's card competes only if it happens to match. Leading is a guess at what your neighbour will choose, and sitting second gives you control of the trick.

variants.title: Blind Spot
variants.hook: Three of your cards were chosen by your opponent, and you can't look at them.
variants.core_twist: Two players. After the deal, each player picks three cards from their own hand and gives them face-down to the opponent as blind cards. On every third trick you must play one of your blind cards unseen, lead or follow. A blind card that fails to follow suit simply loses. You know what you gave and nothing about what you got.

variants.title: You Lead, I Choose
variants.hook: The lead goes round the table in turn. The last trick's winner says which suit must be led.
variants.core_twist: The right to lead passes one seat clockwise each trick, whoever won. The winner of the previous trick names the suit the leader must lead, if they hold it. Winning gives you the choice of battlefield, and someone else chooses the card.

variants.title: Wait and See
variants.hook: Bid now for five points, or watch three tricks first and bid for two.
variants.core_twist: Before the first lead each player either states an exact trick total for five points or holds back. After the third trick, those who held back must bid their final total, for two points if they hit it. Waiting buys information and costs more than half the reward.

variants.title: Endlings
variants.hook: The last card you hold in a suit is worth five more than it says.
variants.core_twist: When you play the final card you hold in a suit, announce it: the card counts five ranks higher. If you later play another card of that suit, you were wrong and lose three points. Short suits become strong ones, and running yourself out of a colour is a plan.

variants.title: Ratchet
variants.hook: In each suit, every card you play has to be higher than your last. Otherwise it's a dud.
variants.core_twist: Each player keeps a marker per suit showing the last rank they played in it. A card played lower than your own marker in that suit goes down face-down and cannot win. You must therefore spend each suit from low to high, and a high card played early kills everything beneath it.
